instructions: Finely chop the mushrooms, half the onion and the red pepper into pieces about the size of a pea.

Melt 1 tbsp of the butter in a 10 inch nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped vegetables and 1/4 tsp salt, and cook for 7 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're soft and the liquid from the mushrooms is gone.
Meanwhile, crack 4 eggs into a bowl. Add 1 tbsp of the milk, 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper, and whisk until smooth. Do the same in a second bowl with the other 4 eggs.
Transfer the vegetables to a bowl and wipe out the skillet.
Melt 1 tbsp butter in the skillet over medium-low heat. Pour in the first bowl of eggs and let the bottom set for 2 to 3 minutes.
Push the cooked edges toward the center with a spatula and tilt the pan so the runny egg flows underneath. Repeat until the top is just glossy and no liquid egg is left.
Sprinkle half the vegetables and 1/2 cup of the cheddar over one half of the omelet. Cook for 30 seconds so the cheese starts to melt.
Fold the empty half over the filling and slide the omelet onto a plate. Cover it with a second plate to keep it warm.
Wipe the skillet, then repeat with the last 1 tbsp butter, the second bowl of eggs, and the rest of the vegetables and cheddar.
Cut each omelet in half to make 4 portions and serve right away.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Live Eat Learn (5.0 from 20 ratings) builds one omelet from sauteed mushrooms, onion and peppers, a little dairy in the eggs, and cheddar melted in before the fold. Baked Bree adds spinach and cooks the vegetables the same way. This is the lead's single omelet scaled to two big omelets cut in half, so four people eat from two turns in the pan, and the vegetables are cooked once and shared. Bell pepper is red only, and the extra vegetables are doubled from the lead's small amounts to make it a dinner. About 28 minutes in all.
